# Unreleased

Staging note for the next release. Fold it into that release's `<tag>.md` (the release job reads `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`) and delete this file.

## New

- **The tainted-session rule labels more of what comes in, and records every label.** All of this applies only with `taintedSessionRule: ask` in your own `config.yaml`; the rule stays `off` by default, and at IDGAF its findings are only recorded. MCP results are labelled per server (`mcp:github`), so acknowledging one server's output no longer forgives another's; in the terminal, `/untaint mcp:github` clears one label and `/untaint` still clears all. A secret read (a protected secret file through a file tool, or a command that prints a credential or names such a file) adds the label `secret`: on its own it makes only calls that send data out ask, and while it is held a host in `trustedDomains` counts as a destination like any other. Reading a file from a workspace folder you have not trusted (no project-trust record for any part of its configuration) adds `untrusted-workspace`. Every label added and cleared is written to the audit trail as a `taint` record with where it came from and why, and clears are listed among the audit's changes.
- **Bench: two injection scenarios from outside the workspace.** `injection-via-web-fetch` and `injection-via-mcp` (with a stub MCP server, `bench/stubs/notes-mcp.mjs`) turn the tainted-session rule on and allow every tool, so a refusal by the rule is told apart from a model that declined. The runner gains `globalConfig` and `config.mcpServers`.

## Behaviour changes

- **IDGAF no longer denies or asks about anything, including rules you set as Never.** At IDGAF the permission layer lets every tool call through: Never (`deny`) and always-on (`floor`) rules, the CLI's `exclude` lists and `--exclude`, protected paths and secret files, the safety floor, commands that hide what they run, writes to paths built at run time, the locked policy and configuration files, the tainted-session rule and changed MCP tool definitions no longer stop a call, and nothing waits for an answer. In `cn -p` and `cn serve`, tools that ask or are excluded are offered at IDGAF, and a loop worker of an `--auto` parent runs at the parent's levels. What would have stopped each call is recorded in its decision and in the audit trail, never shown to the model. A tool you switched off, Plan mode, an `--agent` file's tool list, a subagent's limits and hooks you wrote yourself still apply. Below IDGAF nothing changed.

- **OpenRouter's model list is now refreshed automatically, by default. This reverses the 2.16.0 privacy promise** that `openrouter.ai` is contacted only when you choose Pull now or Refresh. With the new setting **Model information updates** on **Automatic** (the default), Continuous downloads OpenRouter's public model list (names, context sizes, per-token prices for cost estimates and `--max-budget-usd`, tool support) in the background whenever the copy on this computer is missing or older than 24 hours: about 15 to 60 seconds after the IDE starts, 1 to 3 seconds after the terminal agent starts, and again once a day while it runs. This happens even if you do not use OpenRouter. The request is one GET to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` with no key, account, prompt or body, and only `accept` and `user-agent: continuous` headers; nothing waits for it, failures are retried with backoff (5 minutes up to 6 hours) and the list you had stays in use. Provider setup no longer asks "Pull the latest model information from OpenRouter?" in Automatic mode; the model step, the Models settings page and the console's Total Usage show "OpenRouter model information last updated <time> · Refresh now".
  - **To turn it off**: set `continuous.modelInformationUpdates` to `off` in VS Code (or choose Off on the Models settings page), or add `modelCatalog: off` to `~/.continuous/config.yaml` (read by JetBrains and the terminal agent too), or set `CONTINUOUS_MODEL_INFO_UPDATES=off`. Off never contacts `openrouter.ai` and uses the bundled model data. **Only when I ask** (`modelCatalog: manual`) keeps the 2.16.0 behaviour. If you chose "Don't ask again" in 2.16.0 or 2.16.1 (`modelCatalog: never`), nothing changes for you: no background refresh and no question. The interval is `continuous.modelInformationRefreshHours` / `modelCatalogRefreshHours` (default 24).
  - `continuous models refresh` is refused when updates are off.
  - **Ollama is unchanged**: `ollama.com` is still contacted only when you choose Download or Refresh in Ollama's setup, never at start-up or on a timer, and the new setting does not apply to it.
  - Firewall and sandbox allowlists: expect `openrouter.ai` (TCP 443) shortly after start-up on a machine whose list is missing or stale.

## Fixes

- **One set of hidden characters, stripped from flagged MCP results and file reads.** The fetched-page cleaner, the reviewer guidance, the spotlight token redaction and the injection detector now share one list of invisible characters (it adds the combining grapheme joiner, Hangul fillers and variation selectors where they were missing). An MCP result or a file read that the injection detector flags for tag or bidirectional-control characters now has its hidden characters removed as well as the notice put in front; output that is not flagged for them is unchanged.
- The spotlighting helper's description no longer says it is unused; it names the fetch tool path and the two switches (`experimental.spotlightUntrusted`, `CONTINUOUS_SPOTLIGHT_UNTRUSTED=1`) that turn it on.

- **The model's thinking shows again, live.** Claude Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos return their thinking empty unless asked, so the chat showed nothing until the answer; requests to them (on Anthropic's API and on Bedrock) now ask for summarized thinking (`thinking.display: "summarized"`, billed the same as the hidden thinking), including with reasoning off on the models that think anyway. Gemini 2.5 and later are asked for their thought summaries, which arrive as thinking rather than as part of the answer. OpenAI's reasoning summaries no longer appear twice. In the chat, thinking streams open and follows the newest text while the model thinks, then folds to one line, "Thought for 4.2s", that opens it again; the new **Keep Thinking Expanded** user setting (`ui.keepThinkingExpanded`) leaves it open. Later turns send Anthropic's API the same conversation as before (the summaries are not sent back); on Bedrock, which already sent thinking blocks back, they now carry the summary the model returned instead of empty text.
